name: Higashi-Mukojima
tagline: Tokyo in 26 minutes and Otemachi in 26 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000.
summary: The station is in Sumida City, served by Tobu Skytree Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 26 minutes to Otemachi, 40 minutes to Shinjuku, 45 minutes to Shibuya and 39 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. The station stands -0.3 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 0.3 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at -0.3 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from -0.4 m to -0.1 m, a difference of 0.3 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 3 to 5 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 9 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 5 clinics and 4 pharmacies. The nearest hospital is 中林病院, about 7 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 東京都済生会向島病院, about 8 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tobu Skytree Line.
congestion: Tobu Skytree Line runs at 142% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 小菅→北千住, which this station is not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥80,000 to ¥90,000 and 1K ¥100,000 to ¥110,000. 1LDK ¥150,000 to ¥160,000 and 2LDK ¥190,000 to ¥200,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is about average for the 23 wards. What holds the figure down: a large projected flood depth and only one line, the {line}, serving the station. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For quiet, Keisei-Hikifune; for lower rent, Higashi-Mukojima.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Higashi-Mukojima. Keisei-Hikifune has the Keisei Oshiage Line, a different set from Higashi-Mukojima. Journey times to the main business districts are much the same. A one-room flat costs about ¥6,000 more at Keisei-Hikifune. On quiet, Keisei-Hikifune comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Hikifune; for lower rent, Higashi-Mukojima.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Higashi-Mukojima. Hikifune also has the Tobu Kameido Line, which Higashi-Mukojima does not. With more lines, Hikifune is the better connected of the two. Journey times to the main business districts are much the same. A one-room flat, though, costs about ¥11,000 more at Hikifune.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 8 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 1 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tobu Skytree Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
